sections.title: Schemas, ports and the runner
sections.text: Lab 1 separates request validation, execution ports and the runner. The request schema checks browser input. Fixture and live ports share a boundary; run lab one coordinates a turn and its evidence.

sections.title: Router state and origin checks
sections.text: The factory receives a live port and fixture timing. Active maps controllers to unfinished promises; closing blocks new work. The middleware rejects a nonlocal host or mismatched origin with 403 before accepting the query.

sections.title: Validate input and reject overload
sections.text: The query accepts strict JSON up to eight kilobytes. Parsed receives the schema result. Invalid input returns 400. Closing or reaching max concurrent returns 429. These branches stop before selecting an execution port.

sections.title: Choose the execution port
sections.text: Mode, prompt and scenario come from validated data. Live mode calls the injected live port; configuration failure returns 422. Otherwise create fixture port uses scenario and fixture timing. Offline evidence and live provider observations remain distinct.

sections.title: Deadlines and the event stream
sections.text: Deadline milliseconds uses server policy for live work and scenario bounds offline. Abort controller carries cancellation. Open SSE receives that controller and a longer host deadline, leaving time for runner cleanup before transport shutdown.

sections.title: Progress, result and error flow
sections.text: Run lab one receives prompt, port, signal and deadlines. Its emit callback sends progress frames. Result is sent only while the controller is not aborted. A caught failure sends an error; finally ends the stream and removes the active controller.

sections.title: Track work and close cleanly
sections.text: Active retains the work promise before the handler awaits it. The returned close function marks closing, aborts remaining controllers with shutdown, then awaits all settled work. Distinguish progress text from the runner result and confirmed cleanup.

sections.title: Bounded WebSocket teaching bridge
sections.text: Lab 66 uses a local WebSocket bridge around offline or explicitly started Managed work. Command schemas validate messages. Frames, sockets, controllers and acknowledgement maps represent host state; the browser does not receive a provider credential.

sections.title: Backpressure before sending
sections.text: Send first checks that the socket is open. Slow consumer examines buffered bytes; an excessive buffer closes the connection with 1013. JSON is sent only after those checks, preventing an unbounded slow client queue.

sections.title: Sequence and retain frames
sections.text: Emit increments the run sequence and labels each frame with its run and evidence source. It retains at most 64 frames, evicts older entries and updates activity. Closed sockets are removed before broadcasting the new frame.

sections.title: Reconnect with a sequence cursor
sections.text: Replay compares after sequence with the oldest retained frame. If the requested history was evicted, it sends an explicit gap. It then sends only newer frames. Reconnecting cannot recover data the bounded buffer no longer holds.

sections.title: Offline and live execution paths
sections.text: Perform selects the offline fixture or live port. Offline tool results correlate their custom tool event before streaming words. Live work delegates to run lab one with deadlines and a cancellation signal. The reported outcome determines completed, cancelled or error.

sections.title: Authenticate the local upgrade
sections.text: The upgrade checks the exact WebSocket path, local host and origin, an unexpired cookie token, closing state and the eight-client limit. Rejected upgrades write 403 and destroy the socket; accepted ones enter the WebSocket server.

sections.title: Close retained work and transport
sections.text: The returned module exposes router, attach and close. Follow close through controller aborts, settled work and WebSocket shutdown. Local transport closure and confirmed provider interruption are separate evidence boundaries.
